title: Iron Horizon — Anime Mecha Title Slash
description: A hard diagonal split — cobalt vs crimson — pits a silhouetted mecha figure against wall-filling katakana brush type, recreating the freeze-frame title cards of classic mecha OPs. Defined by flat color tension and typographic aggression rather than glow effects or busy texture.
philosophy: This template exists for the single held frame before the action detonates — the intake of breath, the episode number, the name of the unit. It borrows directly from the visual grammar of 1990s–2000s mecha anime: two opposing flat color fields, calligraphic type scaled to fill a half-composition, and a monospace corner tag that signals precision inside chaos. It refuses gradients, lens flares, and any softness that would dilute the compositional violence of the diagonal cut. It is built for speakers who want their opening slide to feel like a cold open, not a cover page.
goodFor: Single-slide reveal moments at developer conferences or product launches
Game studio or anime production pitch deck opening cards
3-word chapter titles requiring maximum visual impact
Showreel or video essay title frames exported as static graphics
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly business reviews requiring readable data
Accessibility-sensitive corporate environments where high-contrast split fields cause distraction
Any slide carrying more than two lines of body copy
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide channels the held freeze-frame before a mecha anime cold open detonates — two flat opposing color fields locked in diagonal tension, no softness, no atmosphere. The silhouetted figure bleeds off three edges to signal scale that the frame cannot contain, while calligraphic type on the opposing field reads as pure graphic mass rather than legible text first. Compositional rhythm is violent and asymmetric: heavy dark form against aggressive typographic fill, void used only where it sharpens the cut. Refuse all glow, lens scatter, gradient fade, or texture — authority here comes entirely from flat color opposition and typographic scale.

examples.layoutNotes: Hard diagonal rule bisects the full canvas from upper-left to lower-right, creating two flat-color zones of near-equal area with no bleed or feathering at the cut. The mecha silhouette occupies the left-lower zone, cropped aggressively at all three frame edges to imply mass that exceeds the slide boundary. Title text — a single dominant line — fills the upper-right zone edge-to-edge at near-maximum column width, functioning as a graphic block rather than a label. A monospace corner tag (unit ID or episode marker) anchors flush to the bottom-right corner with zero padding buffer.

examples.promptCore: This slide should feel like a freeze-frame title card from a mecha cold-open — charged stillness, not decoration. Two opposing flat color fields hold their ground across a hard diagonal seam; the boundary is a confrontation, not a transition. Content lives in sparse, deliberate isolation inside the dominant half while the secondary half erupts with a single overscaled type element that reads as graphic mass before it reads as language. The mood is industrial severity meeting calligraphic aggression — nothing soft, nothing ambient, nothing that glows.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 1920 1080" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet">
  <defs>

  </g>

  <g transform="translate(80,1020)" stroke="#a83232" stroke-width="1.5" fill="none">
    <circle cx="10" cy="10" r="8"/>
    <line x1="0" y1="10" x2="20" y2="10"/>
    <line x1="10" y1="0" x2="10" y2="20"/>
  </g>

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed diagonal split runs lower-left to upper-right with a razor-hard edge — no feathering, no shadow, no overlap zone. The wider left field (roughly 55% of canvas) anchors the content block — a single callout stat, a two-line quote fragment, or a chapter-label + one-line descriptor — at vertical center with an 8% left margin; size contrast alone drives hierarchy, no rule lines needed. The narrower right field fills edge-to-edge with an overscaled typographic element (unit designation, katakana slug, or chapter code) treated as pure graphic mass bleeding off at least two edges. A monospace section-index tag is pinned to the bottom-right outer corner; there is no header band.
